purpose: Harden the GitHub Actions release adapter so registry publication and repository mutation occur only through a narrowly authorized, reviewable release boundary.
scope: .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml and its referenced actions, GitHub Environment configuration documentation, action pinning, permissions, artifact handoff, and workflow tests.
non_goals: Making GitHub Actions the only supported CI or release platform.
Moving provider-neutral release rules from callisto core into workflow shell code.
Requiring Git tag signing in this track; signature policy is covered by SPEC-RELEASE-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-002.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workflow separates unprivileged verification and planning from privileged release execution. The job that can receive registry credentials or write tags/releases is bound to a documented GitHub Environment with required reviewers and branch/tag deployment rules; non-release jobs receive neither registry secrets nor write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN permissions.

Each workflow and job declares the least GitHub token permissions it needs. contents, pull-requests, checks, and statuses are write-scoped only in the job that demonstrably performs that operation; all other jobs default to read or none. A workflow test or policy check rejects an unscoped top-level write grant.

Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable full commit SHAs. A nearby comment records the upstream tag or release used for human review. CI verifies the pin format and fails if an external action reference is changed to a mutable tag or branch.

The planning job uploads the explicit durable plan from SPEC-RELEASE-PLAN-DURABILITY-001 as an artifact. The protected release job downloads only that artifact, verifies its source_commit against its checkout, and fails before credentials are used if validation fails. Caches may accelerate dependency installation but are never read as release intent.

The release trigger and environment policy are documented together: which events may create a version PR, which may publish, who approves publication, and how an emergency rerun is reconciled. A normal push to main cannot silently gain registry publication authority merely because workflow code changed in that push.
